correctness.rationale: Every geodesic-violating triple corresponds to a length-three path of selected edges in K_{3,n}, so faces are exactly star forests. The column-thin subcomplex is the n-fold join of three-point discrete complexes with 2^n top-sphere generators. Every face with a thick column lies in a unique contractible B_j; B_j intersect earlier pieces only through A_n and L_j=A_n intersect B_j is covered by three contractible subcomplexes with pairwise point intersections and no triple intersection. The nerve is S^1, and simple connectivity of A_n for n>=3 nulls each attaching map; homotopy pushouts add n S^2. Relative integral homology and signed join orientations prove the row sign times column-permutation module in H2 for n>=4 and the top augmentation tensor. At n=3 only the stated short exact sequence follows; the n=2 boundary differs. Independent exhaustive geodesic-face and binary boundary tests for n=3 and n=4 yielded 102 and 355 nonempty faces and reduced Betti {2:11} and {2:4,3:16} respectively; finite results are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a full integral homotopy classification, inclusion map, and natural group-module calculation for the natural geodesic general-position complex of the infinite three-row rook-graph family. The additional n two-spheres are structurally forced by thick-column attachments and invisible to the previously published enumerator, while n=3 gives a genuine degree collision and n=2 a distinct boundary.

final_claim: For every n>=3, the graph-geodesic general-position simplicial complex of K_3 square K_n is homotopy equivalent to (2^n copies of S^{n-1}) wedge (n copies of S^2); the integral column-thin inclusion and symmetry modules are specified, with an extension rather than equivariant split at n=3.
limitations: Tests only n=3,4; the all-n proof is the geometric pushout, not finite extrapolation.
Only exactly three rows, n>=3; no equivariant homotopy splitting is claimed.
